sentences.text: Enseosteus is a small member of the class Placodermi, a group of armored fish, and belongs to the family Selenosteidae.
The type species, E. jaekelli, is recognized by a bulbous, knob-shaped rostrum.
The genus was first described by Jaeckel in 1919, with the type species designated as Enseosteus jaekelli.
The name Ottonosteus jaekeli is currently listed as a synonym of Enseosteus.
This animal lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago, in the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Germany and Morocco.
It is debated whether the genus Walterosteus should be synonymized with Enseosteus, as Rücklin (2011) rejects this classification despite Denison's earlier proposal.
